note: The Ṭabaqāt's stories (tabaqat-*): every contradiction tools/grammar_audit.js listed on the new packages, judged by the line. The first run listed 9; one was the author's wording and was corrected in the kit (listed under «corrected»: the conjoined «وَسَلَّمَ» now says its clause is parenthetic like «صَلَّى»'s). Second run: 8 records, all judged here: E = the engine is wrong by the books, C = both readings are allowed.

records.why: «مُلَاءَتَيَّ» is a dual annexed to the speaker's ya (the dual's nūn dropped, its ya merged into the speaker's): a dual in nasb is by the ya — the engine takes the word for a sound singular and asks for a fatḥa.

«وَعَلَى رَقَبَتِهِ أَثْوَابٌ» is a nominal ḥāl clause opened by its wāw (fronted khabar «عَلَى رَقَبَتِهِ», delayed mubtadaʾ «أَثْوَابٌ»); the predicate of «أَصْبَحَ» is «غَادِيًا», already in nasb — the engine reaches past the wāw of the ḥāl.
«اثْنَانِ» is a dual-form noun (mulḥaq bi-l-muthannā): its raf' is by the alif and it never takes tanwin; the engine's «اثْنَانٌ» is not Arabic.

«تِلْكَ شَكَاةٌ ظَاهِرٌ عَنْكَ عَارُهَا»: «ظَاهِرٌ» a sababī naʿt of «شَكَاةٌ» with «عَارُهَا» its doer (the line), or «ظَاهِرٌ» a fronted khabar and «عَارُهَا» its mubtadaʾ, the clause the naʿt (the engine) — both are the grammarians' readings of the half-line; the case (raf') is the same.

«حِينَ أَرَادَ …» hangs on «صَنَعْتُ» (she made the bag when he meant to emigrate); «وَسَلَّمَ» belongs to the parenthetic supplication «صَلَّى اللهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ», which governs nothing outside itself.
«بَعْدَ مَا طُعِنَ» is the time of «دَعَا» (he called for milk after he was stabbed); a proper name «الْخَطَّابِ» carries no taʿalluq and «بَعْدَ» is no naʿt of «لَبَن» here.

«أَنَّ» follows «عَنْ مُحَمَّدٍ» of the isnād in the same printed sentence («… عن أيوب عن محمد أن بلالا …»): «(narrating) that …», so its hamza is opened; the sentence division at «أَنَّ» is ours, and the engine reads it as the head of a sentence.
«أَنَّ» follows «عَنْ أَبِيهِ» of the isnād in the same printed sentence («… عن أبيه أن أهل الشام …»): opened; the sentence division at «أَنَّ» is ours.
